payload.text:
farmers who is trying to sell their produce through online, they will login to the website and will enter the details of what they produced(like crops, vegetables, etc..) for all these the they will give the quantity (kgs), price, yield date, expire date, and current stock location. now the users(buyers) will get all these details by loging to the website. if the user likes the deal then the farmer will accept the request and will transport the stock to the user. here the transportation will be done by the others, like the delivery guy will also login to the website and will see the contract, load(weight of stock), transportation cost, distance, pickup and delivery location. stock money will goes to the farmer and the transportation money will goes to the delivery guy.
here there will be 3 different login interfaces, 1 for farmers login, 1 for buyers login, 1 for the delivery guy.

**Defining the Roles**

I'm now focusing on defining the distinct user roles: Farmer, Buyer, and Delivery. My initial plan is to implement a selection mechanism upon app startup. I'm starting to visualize the "Farmer View" and its crucial components: a dashboard for listings and orders, and a listing creation form.


**Outlining Core Features**

I'm now outlining the features for each user view. The Farmer view will focus on adding produce details, managing orders (accepting/rejecting buyer requests), and viewing an analytical dashboard using recharts. The Buyer view will revolve around browsing the marketplace, filtering/searching, and placing/tracking orders. Finally, the Delivery view centers on viewing contracts, accepting deliveries, and completion. I've also noted a tech stack: React 18+, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Gemini API, lucide-react, and more.
